title: Russian Glide Bombs Kill 11 in Zaporizhzhia After Trump Diesel Deal
excerpt: At least 11 people, including three children, died in early-morning strikes on residential buildings — a day after Washington announced it would buy Russian diesel.
body:
• Russian glide bombs struck residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia in the early hours of Saturday, killing at least 11 people — three of them children — and wounding at least 16, according to regional officials.
  • The strikes landed a day after US President Donald Trump announced a deal with Vladimir Putin to buy Russian diesel, which Kyiv warned would bankroll Moscow's war.
  • "Russia said thank you for the lifting of sanctions on diesel exports by dropping five glide bombs on residential buildings," President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said — this is a separate attack from the Kramatorsk bus-stop and apartment-block strikes covered earlier this week.

Russia struck residential buildings in the southern Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia in the early hours of Saturday, killing at least 11 people, including three children, and wounding at least 16 more, according to regional officials. The attack flattened part of an apartment block while residents slept.

Mykhailo Semikin, the head of the region's military administration, said Russia hit several locations at the same time with aerial bombs. Ivan Fedorov, co-chair of the region's defense council, confirmed at least 16 people were wounded. Rescuers clambered through crumbled masonry to pull residents out alive; one man's leg was trapped in the rubble as workers freed him.

Among the dead was a six-year-old girl whose body rescuers pulled from the wreckage. Her grandfather, Anatoliy Chumniy, stood sobbing over her body, laid on the ground in a white bag. "Her birthday would have been at the end of the month," he said through tears.

Context & Background

Zaporizhzhia, an industrial city with a pre-war population of over 700,000, has been a regular target of Russian bombardment, with strikes intensifying in recent months. Its outskirts lie less than 30 km (20 miles) from the frontline.

https://x.com/sentdefender/status/2108900272332304727

Russia and Ukraine remain locked in a long-range aerial war while their armies are largely deadlocked on the front line, more than four and a half years after Moscow's full-scale invasion. Ukraine is struggling to counter escalating Russian bombardments that have killed scores of civilians in recent days — nearly 80 people died in strikes over two days earlier this week alone. This Zaporizhzhia attack is a distinct, new strike: it is not the Kramatorsk bus-stop bombing reported on October 8 nor the apartment-block missile strike reported on October 9.

Impact & Analysis

The timing of the attack sharpened its political sting. It came a day after Trump said he had struck a deal with Putin to obtain diesel from Russia — 300,000 tons immediately, 500,000 tons in November, one million tons "immediately thereafter," and three million more "within a short period of time" — a stunning reversal of years of US pressure on Moscow over the war and an attempt to address high fuel prices ahead of the November 3 US midterm elections.

Zelenskiy issued some of his sharpest criticism yet of the White House. "Last night became yet another confirmation that Russia perceives any easing of pressure as a signal that it can supposedly keep fighting, that it can supposedly keep dropping bombs on cities. Different signals are needed," he said.

The US Treasury Department moved in parallel, issuing a temporary general license authorizing transactions in Russian-origin diesel through April 7, 2027. Trump's announcement stood in stark contrast to a sweeping Russia sanctions law he signed last month aimed at clamping down on the oil and gas revenues that fuel Russia's war.

What's Next

Rescue operations in Zaporizhzhia were continuing, and the death toll could rise as crews clear the rubble. Meanwhile, US, Ukrainian, and European negotiators held six hours of talks in Miami on Friday on a unified proposal to end the war, covering security guarantees, a post-war economic plan for Ukraine, and territorial questions. Whether the diesel deal undercuts that diplomacy — or simply lowers American fuel prices — will play out in the weeks ahead.
